clue.text: Strip having turned brown bathing in river

indicators.note: something bathing in a river sits inside it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland, and another in Wales and England

indicators.note: having turned says the colour word is read backwards

parts.note: dun is a dull greyish-brown colour

explanation.surface: Someone tanned brown strips off for a swim in the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brown' looks like a suntan, but it is the colour dun, and 'bathing' is the container signal rather than part of the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are verbs for laying bare or removing the covering of something.

clue.text: Spoil mother with advance of years

parts.note: a dam is the mother of an animal, especially a horse
growing older is age

explanation.surface: An old mother spoils her offspring more as the years pass.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: to spoil something is to harm or impair it.

clue.text: Somehow ban novel about resistance using signals to communicate

indicators.note: about means wrapped around, so the scrambled letters surround the other piece
somehow suggests the letters of the two words get into place by some unstated rearrangement

parts.note: R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Banning a novel that is about resistance movements and their secret codes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'concerning' in the surface, but it is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Communication by gesture or signal rather than words is described this way.

clue.text: Curse about engineer briefly coming up in police hunt

indicators.note: the curse goes about, or around, the other piece

parts.note: drat is a mild oath or curse

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the short word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Eng is a short form of engineer

explanation.surface: A cursing detective, short of an engineer, mounts a manhunt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming up' applies only to the short engineer, since this is a down clue; the curse stays the right way round.
explanation.definitionFit: A dragnet is a systematic police search for a wanted person, named after a net dragged through water.

clue.text: Shining silver items thrown out

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
litter is rubbish discarded carelessly

explanation.surface: Bright silverware has been thrown away.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: sparkling or glittering with light.

clue.text: Learn precisely what to do for post in Greendale

definitions.meaning: to learn something word-perfect, by heart

definitions.text: what to do for post in Greendale
definitions.meaning: Postman Pat, a British children's TV postman, works in the village of Greendale; mail is sent off, so this is an instruction to him

explanation.surface: Learning exactly how mail is handled in a fictional village.
explanation.walkthrough: Postman Pat is a British children's TV series about a village postman in Greendale; the second reading is an instruction addressed to Pat to send the post on its way.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for memorising something until it is word-perfect.

clue.text: Some chasing rainbows to fix colour

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some people chase rainbows, hoping to pin down their colours.
explanation.definitionFit: Originally to dye in the grain, fixing colour deep into fibres; now to embed firmly.

clue.text: Note a Gunners headband

parts.note: ti is a note of the sol-fa scale
RA is the Royal Artillery, whose soldiers are gunners

explanation.surface: A note about an Arsenal (the Gunners) football headband.
explanation.walkthrough: The Gunners is also the nickname of Arsenal football club, which helps the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiara is a jewelled ornamental band worn on the head.

clue.text: Provide more weapons for East German last of all

parts.note: to rearm is to arm again
Ost is the German word for east

explanation.surface: Rearming East Germany is the lowest priority.
explanation.definitionFit: The furthest back, so the very last in position.

clue.text: Crazy person from Northern Ireland area absorbed in computer

indicators.note: absorbed in means taken inside, so these letters go within the computer

parts.note: a Mac is an Apple computer

explanation.surface: A madman from Belfast way is glued to his computer screen.
explanation.definitionFit: A maniac is a wildly unhinged or obsessive individual.

clue.text: Greek character cheers collecting ultimately excellent marks

indicators.note: collecting means taking in, so the letter goes inside the Greek one

parts.note: sigma is a letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the next word

parts.note: ta is British informal for thanks

explanation.surface: A Greek is cheered for collecting excellent grades.
explanation.definitionFit: Stigmata are marks, especially the wounds of Christ appearing on a body.

clue.text: Rebel gent in revolution protected country

indicators.note: something in revolution is turned over and reordered, so the letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: A rebellious gentleman joins a revolution in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: A green belt is a British planning term for a ring of land around a town protected from building.
explanation.definitionFit: A zone of open land where development is restricted by planning law.

clue.text: Curses director perhaps with shares

parts.note: a director is an example of an exec, a company executive
rations are allotted shares

explanation.surface: A director swears about his shareholding.
explanation.definitionFit: Execrations are loud denunciations or oaths, so synonyms of curses as nouns.

clue.text: Gangster with weapon creates panic

parts.note: Al Capone is the archetypal gangster
an arm is a weapon, as in firearm

explanation.surface: An armed mobster spreads fear.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: sudden fear or anxiety at danger.

clue.text: Refined frigid brunettes I'd abandoned — one wouldn't make much of a catch!

definitions.text: one wouldn't make much of a catch!

indicators.note: refined means reworked into a new form, so the letters are rearranged
abandoned says the letters of the short word are left out of the pool before rearranging

explanation.surface: Posh, cold brunettes are abandoned, as none would be a good catch as a partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refined' rearranges FRIGID BRUNETTES once 'abandoned' has removed I and D. The surface 'catch' is a suitor; the real one is a cricket ball.
explanation.definitionFit: A clumsy person who drops things, such as a fielder who fumbles a ball.

clue.text: Person in Crowd Scene One in movie, concealing head — fan?

parts.note: an extra is a background performer in a film crowd

indicators.note: concealing the head means the first letter is hidden away

parts.note: an actor is someone appearing in a film

explanation.surface: A film extra hides her face behind a fan.
explanation.definitionFit: An extractor fan draws stale air or smoke out of a room.

clue.text: Classic sports car — Micra's crashed catching it

indicators.note: catching means holding inside, so the scrambled letters surround the other word
a crashed car is wrecked, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A Nissan Micra crashes into a classic sports car.
explanation.walkthrough: The Reliant Scimitar was a British sports car of the 1960s and 70s; the curved sword sense is not the one defined here.
explanation.definitionFit: The Reliant Scimitar is a well-known British sports coupé from the 1960s and 1970s.

clue.text: Producer of decorative writing a spiral glitch ruined

indicators.note: ruined means wrecked, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A penman's flourish is spoilt by a spiralling slip of the pen.
explanation.definitionFit: A practitioner of fine ornamental handwriting.

clue.text: This month everyone gets put in place

parts.note: inst. (instant) is an old business abbreviation for this month
all means everybody

explanation.surface: This month, everyone gets settled in.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: to set something up in position.

clue.text: Nice tax breaks as a ballpark figure

indicators.note: breaks says the words are broken up and their letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Tax breaks in Nice are only estimated roughly.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballpark figure is a rough estimate, so approximate or imprecise.

clue.text: Pay agriculture department unknown amount

parts.note: DEFRA is the UK Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs
y is a mathematical unknown

explanation.surface: Paying the farming ministry an unspecified sum.
explanation.definitionFit: To defray is to meet the cost of something, to settle it.

clue.text: Scoffs at examinations

definitions.meaning: in British schools, ... are practice exams taken before the real ones

explanation.surface: Pupils sneer at their exams.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain, mocks are practice exams sat before the real ones.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a verb for jeering; the other is British school slang for trial tests.

clue.text: Piece of bric-a-brac made of copper and gold turned up around India

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: around means placed about another piece, enclosing it
in a down clue, turned up means read from the bottom upward

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry
I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A trinket of copper and gold comes to light, made in India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' makes RO from OR, and 'around' puts RO around I.
explanation.definitionFit: A curio is a small unusual collectable object, a knick-knack.

clue.text: Front of book, e.g. Master and Servant

parts.note: Master is an example of a title, a form of address
a page is a boy servant

explanation.surface: The cover of a novel called Master and Servant.
explanation.definitionFit: The leaf at the start of a book bearing its name and author.

clue.text: Temperature right in old Spanish kingdom to produce aromatic herb

indicators.note: in places this letter inside the kingdom's name

parts.note: Aragon was a medieval kingdom in north-east Spain

explanation.surface: Warm weather in old Spain grows a fragrant herb.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarragon is a culinary herb with an aniseed scent.

clue.text: Bird of prey — something normally seen over hill

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: par is the normal or expected level
a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A hawk is a common sight hovering over a hill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'normally seen' points to par, the usual standard, as in 'up to par'; 'over' then reverses it in this across clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A raptor is a hunting bird such as an eagle, hawk or falcon.

clue.text: Looks for food and shelter initially having no fixed abode

parts.note: to rootle is to dig about for food, as a pig does with its snout

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A homeless person scavenges for food and shelter.
explanation.definitionFit: Without roots or a settled home, wandering.

clue.text: Strapping king in private room

indicators.note: in puts the king letter inside the room

parts.note: a study is a private room for reading and work
R is the abbreviation for rex, king

explanation.surface: A burly monarch sits in his den.
explanation.definitionFit: Strapping means robust and well-built, as is a synonym here.
